card.title: Make It Their Idea
card.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have such a good eye for storage. Sorting our shed could finally give your tools a proper home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Until you dump paint tins everywhere again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could assign every shelf. I'd follow your labels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Including a shelf you're forbidden to touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. You could put it at eye level so I see what I'm missing.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes sorting promise a tool home, A3 offers lasting labeling control and A5 accepts an untouchable shelf to sweeten the role.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 prior dumping prompts A3 compliance promise; B4 exclusive-shelf request causes A5 eye-level protected space.

relationship.evidence: B2 doubts the lasting benefit and B4 tests whether real authority will accompany the chore.

heightening.evidence: B4 demand for protected space receives A5 an extra visible guarantee of control, making volunteering more attractive.

specificity.evidence: A1 shared shed and B2 paint-tin habit establish the chore and why B resists.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 seeing what I am missing makes A's own exclusion an earned selling point.
